META-ABSTRACT

META-ABSTRACT

C. CODE ARCHITECTURE is the computational branch of 2. RP9. EXPANSION.

Its function is to collect the executable controls, exact calculations, machine-level measurements, generated output, and traceable computational records assigned to the Expansion without converting those computational positions into a new functional origin.

The branch contains four Expansion code-package positions: 0. CODE 0, A. CODE 1, B. CODE 2, and C. CODE 3, together with D. RP9. RIEMANN SUBMISSION CODE PACK as a local reference-copy position.

0. CODE 0 contains four independent Rx8 validators. A. CODE 1 executes the first-differentiation control. B. CODE 2 executes the residual-value control. C. CODE 3 contains the updated CODE 4 — META EQUILIBRIUM RELATIONAL VALIDATOR, replacing the previous K007 secondary alpha positioning. D. RP9. RIEMANN SUBMISSION CODE PACK provides local access to copies of K.6, K.7, and K.8 from the Submission, with bulk K.7 prime-position data omitted.

These packages are grouped by computational function and repository position. Their folder order provides stable reading and navigation access; it does not establish a mandatory execution dependency between the packages.

4. PACKAGE A — CODE 1

FIRST DIFFERENTIATION

A. CODE 1 contains:

PYTHON CODE ID: CODE 1
EXECUTABLE: CODE_1.py
OFFICIAL CODE TITLE: CODE 1. RP9 FIRST DIFFERENTIATION — REVISED
OUTPUT DIRECTORY: 2. OUTPUT

Its assigned computational position isolates and executes the first-differentiation control.

Version 2.1.0 passes calculated results through the positional-to-intersection-to-quotient sequence and includes eight control areas. It records data, trace, verification, control, report, audit, and execution-log outputs. Machine diagnostics include float probes and neighboring representable values.

Its position within C. CODE ARCHITECTURE is independent of the Rx8 validator package and does not require CODE 0 to execute as a runtime prerequisite.

5. PACKAGE B — CODE 2

RESIDUAL VALUE

B. CODE 2 contains:

PYTHON CODE ID: CODE 2
EXECUTABLE: CODE 2.py
OFFICIAL CODE TITLE: CODE 2. RP9 RESIDUAL VALUE
OUTPUT DIRECTORY: 2. OUTPUT

Its assigned computational position measures the binary machine-scale quotient around 1.0 and verifies the three-step binary scale relation.

The recorded relation is:

𝑅15/𝑅16=23=8

The package separates measured machine relations from downstream interpretation and records its own execution result independently.

Its current output architecture is assigned to local 2. OUTPUT.

6. PACKAGE C — CODE 3

META EQUILIBRIUM RELATIONAL VALIDATOR — CODE 4

C. CODE 3 retains its repository folder position and contains the updated executable:

PYTHON CODE ID: CODE4
EXECUTABLE: CODE_4.py
PROGRAM TITLE: CODE 4 — META EQUILIBRIUM RELATIONAL VALIDATOR
VERSION: 2.1.0
OUTPUT DIRECTORY: 2. OUTPUT

The folder name identifies the repository position. The executable identity remains CODE 4.

This validator replaces the previous K007 secondary alpha-positioning operation.

Its 17 controls examine exact complementary and reciprocal relations, binary normalization, equivalent quotient representations, functional position assignments, Base-10 scale projection, binary machine-scale behavior, and arithmetic consistency of calculated positions.

The additional positional calculations use outputs already calculated within the program:

CALCULATED POSITION PAIRS
        ↓
EXACT DIFFERENCE
        ↓
ARITHMETIC RECONSTRUCTION / RELATIVE QUOTIENT / POSITIONAL ORDER
        ↓
EXACT TERMINATING DECIMAL ROUNDTRIP

No externally supplied alpha decimal continuation is used as calculation input.

The program generates CODE4_CONTROL.txt, CODE4_DATA.json, and CODE4_REPORT.md. Its aggregate result is COMPLETE RELATIONAL LOCK when all implemented controls pass, or RELATIONAL BREAK when a control fails.

The local README provides the detailed control descriptions and their interpretation.

7. PACKAGE D — RIEMANN SUBMISSION CODE PACK

LOCAL SUBMISSION CODE-REFERENCE COPY

D. RP9. RIEMANN SUBMISSION CODE PACK provides local access to copies of the Submission's K.6, K.7, and K.8 packages.

Their primary source location is:

1. RP9. THE RIEMANN SUBMISSION / A. RP9. THE RIEMANN SUBMISSION / SECTION. 3

The Expansion copy supports informational access and relational comparison with the Expansion's computational material.

Bulk K.7 prime-position data associated with the recorded genealogy through 100,000,000,000 are omitted from this reference copy. The final report, code, and remaining supporting records are retained.

This reduces duplicated storage while preserving local access to the reported results and computational sources. The retained report describes its recorded execution; the omitted bulk dataset is not available in this local copy.

Read D. INFO — RP9. RIEMANN SUBMISSION CODE PACK for the purpose, source location, and storage boundary of the reference copy.

11. RELATION TO THE EXPANSION

C. CODE ARCHITECTURE is one of the parallel downstream branches of 2. RP9. EXPANSION.

Its assigned perspective is computational.

It receives already established informational, relational, positional, scalar, or representational material where required by a local executable and subjects that material to its assigned calculation or control.

The branch relation is therefore:

ESTABLISHED BASIS
        ↓
MULTIPLE AVAILABLE CONSEQUENCES
        ↓
COMPUTATIONAL READING / CONTROL

not:

CODE
        ↓
NEW ORIGIN
        ↓
NEW PRIMARY FUNCTION

INFORMATIONAL CONNECTION≠SEQUENTIAL DEPENDENCY

and:

PARALLEL FUNCTIONAL ARCHITECTURE≠SEQUENTIAL DERIVATIONAL CHAIN

12. MRF AND REVIEW ACCESS

The local 000. A.P.X. 2.C position provides machine-readable aggregation and navigation material for C. CODE ARCHITECTURE.

The MRF is a review and transport representation of the source material.

It does not replace the original package files, executable sources, or generated outputs.

The authority remains with the identifiable local source and its corresponding execution record.

Therefore:

MRF=AGGREGATED REVIEW ACCESS≠SOURCE REPLACEMENT

13. SECTION BOUNDARY

C. CODE ARCHITECTURE provides computational execution and computational evidence for assigned Expansion positions.

It does not operate as:

A NEW PRIMARY DERIVATION

A MASTER EXECUTION CONTROLLER

A SINGLE COMBINED PASS / FAIL ENGINE

A REQUIRED SEQUENTIAL CODE CHAIN

A REPLACEMENT FOR THE SOURCE MATERIAL

The individual packages remain distinguishable by function, source, execution, and result.

Their common placement under C. CODE ARCHITECTURE establishes repository organization and computational review access, not a new dependency relation.

The complete section relation is:

ONE ESTABLISHED EXPANSION BASIS↓MULTIPLE COMPUTATIONAL POSITIONS↓DISTINGUISHABLE EXECUTABLE OPERATIONS↓SELF-CONTAINED EXECUTION WHERE ASSIGNED↓TRACEABLE COMPUTATIONAL RESULTS

with:

COMPUTATIONAL POSITION≠FUNCTIONAL ORIGIN

META-ABSTRACT

META-ABSTRACT

0. CODE 0 is the computational validation package assigned to the Rx8 material within the PBF Expansion.

The package contains four distinguishable validator functions:

  • genealogical validation;
  • proportion-structure validation;
  • functional-relation validation;
  • residual and representation validation.

Each validator is a self-contained computational unit with its own executable source, internal controls, generated output, verification material, trace material, audit material, and presentation layer.

The four validators are grouped because they examine related Rx8 information from different computational positions.

Their grouping does not create a combined execution system.

Their numerical labels provide stable package identification and reading order only.

No validator requires another validator to execute or establish its own assigned result.

README — 1. RP9. RX8

RP9 RX8 GENEALOGICAL VALIDATOR

PYTHON CODE ID
RX8. A

FILESYSTEM
RX8. A.py

OFFICIAL CODE TITLE
RX8. RP9 RX8 GENEALOGICAL VALIDATOR

The short filesystem name does not replace or shorten the official code title.

1. Purpose

This code is a self-contained Rx8 genealogical validator.

Its purpose is to verify the internally defined genealogical structure of the Rx8 model and to ensure that later defined positions remain assigned to their derived roles rather than being reassigned as origin positions.

The validator therefore performs one independent function:

GENEALOGICAL CONSISTENCY CONTROL

It does not require another RP9 code, validator, controller, or combined execution package in order to execute or produce its assigned result.

2. Which function is verified

The code verifies:

GENEALOGY

The internal structure tested is:

Origin
↓
Derivation
↓
Representation
↓
Reconstruction
↓
Residual

The code evaluates the consistency of these assigned positions within its own defined model.

It does not perform numerical optimization or depend on external reference systems.

3. What the code tests

The code verifies six checkpoints:

1. Position of the first relation

2. Derivation status of the first representation

3. That the representation does not claim a new origin relation

4. Rx8 as reconstruction

5. Residual layer position

6. That no later defined layer claims origin status

The internally defined chain checked is:

RELATION
1/3 ↔ 2/3

↓

REPRESENTATION
1/4 ↔ 3/4

↓

RX8
2R × 4 = 8R

↓

RESIDUAL
Representational trace

The code tests the internal consistency of this declared genealogical structure.

4. Why this code is relevant

Within the Rx8 material, relation, representation, reconstruction, and residual occupy distinguishable informational positions.

The code therefore applies the following internal rule:

RELATION BEFORE PROJECTION

The assigned genealogy is:

Relation
↓
Representation
↓
Rx8
↓
Residual

Within this defined model, no subsequent node may:

1. Lack an assigned derivation source

2. Claim origin status

3. Replace the defined origin relation

The function of the code is therefore not to create the genealogy, but to test whether the genealogy encoded inside the program remains internally consistent with these assignments.

5. Verification model

The verification is based on four defined layers:

RELATION

REPRESENTATION

RECONSTRUCTION

RESIDUAL

For the relevant nodes, the code evaluates:

Source of derivation

Layer status

Origin claim

Internal consistency

The code independently generates:

DATA

TRACE

AUDIT

VERIFY

PRESENTATION

CONTROL LOG

These outputs provide separate machine-readable and human-readable records of the same execution.

No output from another RP9 code is required.

6. Expected result

For the test to pass:

RELATION_ORIGIN_1

must remain the only internally defined node permitted to carry:

PRIMARY_ORIGIN_RELATION

while:

REPRESENTATION_1

RX8_CAPSULATION_1

RESIDUAL_1

must retain valid derivation assignments and must not claim origin status.

Expected final status:

PASS

7. Actual result

All six verification steps passed:

Check Result
VERIFY_FIRST_RELATION_POSITION PASS
DERIVE_FIRST_REPRESENTATION PASS
CHECK_NO_NEW_RELATION_CREATED PASS
VALIDATE_RX8_CAPSULATION PASS
VALIDATE_RESIDUAL_LAYER PASS
FAIL_IF_LATER_LAYER_INTRODUCES_UNGROUNDED_RELATION PASS

The audit report shows:

Expected number of origin relations: 1

Observed number of origin relations: 1

Later layers claiming origin: 0

Final status:

PASS

8. Conclusion

The validator passed all six of its internally defined checks.

Within the model encoded by this code:

1/3 ↔ 2/3

remains the defined origin relation.

The representation:

1/4 ↔ 3/4

remains assigned as derived.

Rx8 remains assigned as reconstruction.

The residual remains assigned as representational trace.

No later defined node introduces or claims a new primary relation.

The result therefore establishes that the genealogy encoded by this validator is internally consistent according to the validator's stated criteria.

9. Files Created

When run, the code independently generates:

2. OUTPUT

├── RX8.A_DATA.json
├── RX8.A_TRACE.json
├── RX8.A_AUDIT.json
├── RX8.A_VERIFY.json
├── RX8.A_REPORT.md
└── RX8.A_CONTROL.txt

Each output has a distinct reporting function:

RX8.A_DATA.json = structured execution data

RX8.A_TRACE.json = execution and verification trace

RX8.A_AUDIT.json = origin-claim audit

RX8.A_VERIFY.json = machine-readable verification flags

RX8.A_REPORT.md = human-readable result

RX8.A_CONTROL.txt = execution log

All outputs are produced by this code from its own execution.

10. Relation to other Rx8 codes

Other codes in the Rx8 code architecture may test different properties of the same broader Rx8 material.

For example, a separate code may test proportional structure while this code tests genealogical consistency.

These are related informational functions, not execution dependencies.

GENEALOGICAL CONTROL
=
INDEPENDENT EXECUTION
+
INDEPENDENT RESULT

and:

PROPORTIONAL CONTROL
=
SEPARATE INDEPENDENT EXECUTION
+
SEPARATE INDEPENDENT RESULT

Therefore:

RELATED INFORMATIONAL FUNCTION
≠
CROSS-CODE EXECUTION DEPENDENCY

No subsequent validator is required to confirm that this code executed correctly, and this code is not required for another independent code to execute correctly.

Its assigned result stands on its own execution.

SELF-CONTAINED CODE
↓
SELF-CONTAINED EXECUTION
↓
SELF-CONTAINED OUTPUT
↓
SELF-CONTAINED RESULT

Cross-code comparison may occur at the informational, documentation, database, or review level.

It is not part of this code's execution requirement.

Therefore:

≠

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# RP9_CODE_ID: C.0070
# =============================================================================
# RP9. CODE IDENTITY
#
# REPOSITORY: RP9. RH. Z0
#     2. RP9. EXPANSION

# =============================================================================

# RP9_RX8_GENEALOGICAL_VALIDATOR.py
# Version: 1.1.0
# Purpose:
# Validate Rx8 as a genealogical derivation chain.
# This script writes what is tested, how it is tested, why it is tested, and the final result.
# Output is written to both Markdown and JSON.

import json
import math
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path

PYTHON_CODE_ID = "RX8. A"
FILE_NAME = "RX8. A.py"
OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE = "RX8. RP9 RX8 GENEALOGICAL VALIDATOR"
SCRIPT_VERSION = "1.1.0"

OUTPUT_DIR_NAME = "2. OUTPUT"
DATA_FILE = "RX8.A_DATA.json"
TRACE_FILE = "RX8.A_TRACE.json"
AUDIT_FILE = "RX8.A_AUDIT.json"
VERIFY_FILE = "RX8.A_VERIFY.json"
REPORT_FILE = "RX8.A_REPORT.md"
CONTROL_FILE = "RX8.A_CONTROL.txt"


def now_iso():
    return datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def make_output_dir():
    out_dir = Path.cwd() / OUTPUT_DIR_NAME
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return out_dir


def write_text(path, content):
    path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")


def write_json(path, data):
    path.write_text(json.dumps(data, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False), encoding="utf-8")


def fraction_to_text(value):
    if isinstance(value, Fraction):
        return str(value)
    return str(value)


def status_from_bool(value):
    if value:
        return "PASS"
    return "FAIL"


def make_record(step_id, title, what_is_tested, how_it_is_tested, why_it_is_tested, passed, final_result, data=None):
    return {
        "step_id": step_id,
        "title": title,
        "what_is_tested": what_is_tested,
        "how_it_is_tested": how_it_is_tested,
        "why_it_is_tested": why_it_is_tested,
        "status": status_from_bool(passed),
        "final_result": final_result,
        "data": data or {}
    }


def validate_first_relation():
    relation = {
        "id": "RELATION_ORIGIN_1",
        "layer": "RELATION",
        "name": "FIRST_RELATIONAL_DIFFERENTIATION",
        "left": Fraction(1, 3),
        "right": Fraction(2, 3),
        "total": Fraction(1, 1),
        "claim": "PRIMARY_ORIGIN_RELATION",
        "derived_from": None,
        "may_claim_origin": True
    }

    passed = (
        relation["left"] + relation["right"] == relation["total"]
        and relation["left"] == Fraction(1, 3)
        and relation["right"] == Fraction(2, 3)
        and relation["may_claim_origin"] is True
    )

    data = {
        "left": fraction_to_text(relation["left"]),
        "right": fraction_to_text(relation["right"]),
        "sum": fraction_to_text(relation["left"] + relation["right"]),
        "claim": relation["claim"],
        "may_claim_origin": relation["may_claim_origin"]
    }

    final_result = "First relation is locked as origin." if passed else "First relation failed origin validation."

    record = make_record(
        "1",
        "VERIFY_FIRST_RELATION_POSITION",
        "The first relation position 1/3 <-> 2/3.",
        "The script verifies that 1/3 + 2/3 = 1 and that this node alone may claim origin status.",
        "This prevents later representations from being mistaken for the first relation.",
        passed,
        final_result,
        data
    )

    return relation, record


def derive_first_representation(relation):
    representation = {
        "id": "REPRESENTATION_1",
        "layer": "REPRESENTATION",
        "name": "FIRST_FRACTAL_REPRESENTATION",
        "active": Fraction(3, 4),
        "reference": Fraction(1, 4),
        "total": Fraction(1, 1),
        "claim": "DERIVED_REPRESENTATION",
        "derived_from": relation["id"],
        "may_claim_origin": False
    }

    passed = (
        representation["active"] + representation["reference"] == representation["total"]
        and representation["derived_from"] == relation["id"]
        and representation["may_claim_origin"] is False
    )

    data = {
        "active": fraction_to_text(representation["active"]),
        "reference": fraction_to_text(representation["reference"]),
        "sum": fraction_to_text(representation["active"] + representation["reference"]),
        "derived_from": representation["derived_from"],
        "claim": representation["claim"],
        "may_claim_origin": representation["may_claim_origin"]
    }

    final_result = "First representation is derived and does not claim origin." if passed else "First representation failed derivation validation."

    record = make_record(
        "2",
        "DERIVE_FIRST_REPRESENTATION",
        "The first representation 1/4 <-> 3/4.",
        "The script verifies that 1/4 + 3/4 = 1 and that the representation is derived from RELATION_ORIGIN_1.",
        "This locks representation as after-construction, not as a new primary relation.",
        passed,
        final_result,
        data
    )

    return representation, record


def check_representation_does_not_create_new_relation(relation, representation):
    passed = (
        representation["derived_from"] == relation["id"]
        and representation["may_claim_origin"] is False
        and representation["claim"] != "PRIMARY_ORIGIN_RELATION"
    )

    data = {
        "origin_relation": relation["id"],
        "representation": representation["id"],
        "representation_claim": representation["claim"],
        "representation_may_claim_origin": representation["may_claim_origin"]
    }

    final_result = "Representation did not create a new primary relation." if passed else "Representation incorrectly introduced or claimed a new primary relation."

    return make_record(
        "3",
        "CHECK_NO_NEW_RELATION_CREATED",
        "Whether representation creates a new relation.",
        "The script checks that the representation remains derived, cannot claim origin, and does not use PRIMARY_ORIGIN_RELATION as its claim.",
        "This is the lock against circular self-confirmation and false origin transfer.",
        passed,
        final_result,
        data
    )


def validate_rx8_capsulation(representation):
    rx8 = {
        "id": "RX8_CAPSULATION_1",
        "layer": "RECONSTRUCTION",
        "name": "R_TIMES_8_CAPSULATION",
        "R": "symbolic_R_not_measured",
        "diameter_coefficient": Fraction(2, 1),
        "square_sides": 4,
        "perimeter_coefficient": Fraction(8, 1),
        "derived_from": representation["id"],
        "claim": "CAPSULATION_RECONSTRUCTION",
        "may_claim_origin": False
    }

    calculated_perimeter = rx8["diameter_coefficient"] * rx8["square_sides"]

    passed = (
        calculated_perimeter == rx8["perimeter_coefficient"]
        and rx8["perimeter_coefficient"] == Fraction(8, 1)
        and rx8["derived_from"] == representation["id"]
        and rx8["may_claim_origin"] is False
    )

    data = {
        "R_status": rx8["R"],
        "diameter": "2R",
        "square_sides": rx8["square_sides"],
        "calculated_perimeter": "8R",
        "perimeter_coefficient": fraction_to_text(rx8["perimeter_coefficient"]),
        "derived_from": rx8["derived_from"],
        "may_claim_origin": rx8["may_claim_origin"]
    }

    final_result = "Rx8 is validated as capsulation and reconstruction." if passed else "Rx8 capsulation failed validation."

    record = make_record(
        "4",
        "VALIDATE_RX8_CAPSULATION",
        "Rx8 as R x 8 capsulation.",
        "The script keeps R symbolic and verifies that four square sides of 2R create 8R without measuring R.",
        "This shows Rx8 as reconstruction of R, not as a new origin value.",
        passed,
        final_result,
        data
    )

    return rx8, record


def validate_residual_belongs_to_representation(representation):
    exact_ratio = Fraction(3, 4)
    exact_lock = Fraction(1, 4)

    ri_float = math.sqrt(3.0) / 2.0
    ratio_observed = ri_float * ri_float
    lock_observed = 1.0 - ratio_observed

    ratio_expected = float(exact_ratio)
    lock_expected = float(exact_lock)

    ratio_residual = ratio_observed - ratio_expected
    lock_residual = lock_observed - lock_expected
    symmetric_residual = math.isclose(ratio_residual + lock_residual, 0.0, rel_tol=0.0, abs_tol=1e-30)
    exact_relation_preserved = exact_ratio + exact_lock == Fraction(1, 1)

    residual = {
        "id": "RESIDUAL_1",
        "layer": "RESIDUAL",
        "name": "FLOAT_REPRESENTATION_RESIDUAL",
        "derived_from": representation["id"],
        "claim": "REPRESENTATION_TRACE",
        "may_claim_origin": False,
        "ratio_residual": ratio_residual,
        "lock_residual": lock_residual,
        "symmetric_residual": symmetric_residual
    }

    passed = (
        residual["derived_from"] == representation["id"]
        and residual["may_claim_origin"] is False
        and symmetric_residual is True
        and exact_relation_preserved is True
    )

    data = {
        "exact_ratio": fraction_to_text(exact_ratio),
        "exact_lock": fraction_to_text(exact_lock),
        "exact_sum": fraction_to_text(exact_ratio + exact_lock),
        "ratio_observed_float": format(ratio_observed, ".20e"),
        "lock_observed_float": format(lock_observed, ".20e"),
        "ratio_residual": format(ratio_residual, ".20e"),
        "lock_residual": format(lock_residual, ".20e"),
        "symmetric_residual": symmetric_residual,
        "residual_layer": residual["layer"],
        "derived_from": residual["derived_from"],
        "may_claim_origin": residual["may_claim_origin"]
    }

    final_result = "Residual is isolated to representation and exact relation remains unchanged." if passed else "Residual isolation failed."

    record = make_record(
        "5",
        "VALIDATE_RESIDUAL_LAYER",
        "Whether float residual belongs to representation.",
        "The script compares exact 3/4 and 1/4 against float-derived values and checks symmetric residual cancellation.",
        "This proves residual as representation trace, not as a mutation of the relation.",
        passed,
        final_result,
        data
    )

    return residual, record


def validate_no_ungrounded_later_origin(nodes):
    failures = []

    for node in nodes:
        if node["layer"] != "RELATION":
            if node.get("may_claim_origin") is True:
                failures.append({
                    "node_id": node["id"],
                    "reason": "Later layer claims origin."
                })
            if node.get("derived_from") is None:
                failures.append({
                    "node_id": node["id"],
                    "reason": "Later layer has no derivation source."
                })

    passed = len(failures) == 0

    data = {
        "checked_nodes": [node["id"] for node in nodes],
        "failures": failures
    }

    final_result = "No later layer introduced an ungrounded primary relation." if passed else "Ungrounded later relation detected."

    return make_record(
        "6",
        "FAIL_IF_LATER_LAYER_INTRODUCES_UNGROUNDED_RELATION",
        "Whether any later layer introduces an ungrounded origin relation.",
        "The script scans every non-relation node and fails if it claims origin or lacks a derivation source.",
        "This is the final lock: no after-construction may be promoted into origin.",
        passed,
        final_result,
        data
    )


def normalize_nodes_for_json(nodes):
    cleaned = []
    for node in nodes:
        item = {}
        for key, value in node.items():
            if isinstance(value, Fraction):
                item[key] = str(value)
            else:
                item[key] = value
        cleaned.append(item)
    return cleaned

def build_log(records, out_dir, global_status):
    lines = []
    lines.append("RP9 RX8 GENEALOGICAL VALIDATOR LOG")
    lines.append("Generated: " + now_iso())

    lines.append("Output directory: " + str(out_dir))

    lines.append("")
    for record in records:
        lines.append(record["step_id"] + " | " + record["status"] + " | " + record["title"] + " | " + record["final_result"])
    lines.append("")
    return "\n".join(lines)


def run_validator():
    out_dir = make_output_dir()
    trace = []
    nodes = []

    relation, record_1 = validate_first_relation()
    trace.append(record_1)
    nodes.append(relation)

    representation, record_2 = derive_first_representation(relation)
    trace.append(record_2)
    nodes.append(representation)

    record_3 = check_representation_does_not_create_new_relation(relation, representation)
    trace.append(record_3)

    rx8, record_4 = validate_rx8_capsulation(representation)
    trace.append(record_4)
    nodes.append(rx8)

    residual, record_5 = validate_residual_belongs_to_representation(representation)
    trace.append(record_5)
    nodes.append(residual)

    record_6 = validate_no_ungrounded_later_origin(nodes)
    trace.append(record_6)

    global_pass = all(record["status"] == "PASS" for record in trace)
    global_status = status_from_bool(global_pass)

    summary = {
        "repository": "RP9. RH. Z0",
        "repository_branch": "2. RP9. EXPANSION",
        "python_code_id": PYTHON_CODE_ID,
        "filesystem_name": FILE_NAME,
        "official_code_title": OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE,
        "version": SCRIPT_VERSION,

        "global_status": global_status,
        "what_is_tested": "Rx8 as a genealogical derivation from the first relation.",
        "how_it_is_tested": "Every later layer must be derived and must not claim origin status.",
        "why_it_is_tested": "To lock relation before projection and prevent after-constructions from becoming origin claims.",
        "final_result": "PASS means the genealogy is locked. FAIL means an ungrounded later relation was introduced."
    }

    data_payload = {
        "SUMMARY": summary,
        "NODES": normalize_nodes_for_json(nodes),
        "TRACE": trace
    }

    audit_payload = {
        "AUDIT": {
            "what_is_tested": "Audit of origin claims across all layers.",
            "how_it_is_tested": "Counts origin-capable relation nodes and checks later layers for illegal origin claims.",
            "why_it_is_tested": "Only the first relation may carry origin status.",
            "no_competing_relation_search": True,
            "genealogical_validation_only": True,
            "origin_relation_count_expected": 1,
            "origin_relation_count_observed": len([node for node in nodes if node["layer"] == "RELATION" and node.get("may_claim_origin") is True]),
            "later_origin_claims": [
                node["id"] for node in nodes
                if node["layer"] != "RELATION" and node.get("may_claim_origin") is True
            ],
            "global_status": global_status,
            "final_result": global_status
        }
    }

    verify_payload = {
        "VERIFY": {
            "what_is_tested": "Machine-readable final verification flags.",
            "how_it_is_tested": "Each step must return PASS for global PASS.",
            "why_it_is_tested": "This gives a direct audit surface for external review.",
            "first_relation_locked": record_1["status"] == "PASS",
            "first_representation_derived": record_2["status"] == "PASS",
            "representation_does_not_create_new_relation": record_3["status"] == "PASS",
            "rx8_is_capsulation": record_4["status"] == "PASS",
            "residual_belongs_to_representation": record_5["status"] == "PASS",
            "no_ungrounded_later_relation": record_6["status"] == "PASS",
            "global_status": global_status,
            "final_result": global_status
        }
    }

    write_json(out_dir / DATA_FILE, data_payload)
    write_json(out_dir / TRACE_FILE, {"TRACE": trace})
    write_json(out_dir / AUDIT_FILE, audit_payload)
    write_json(out_dir / VERIFY_FILE, verify_payload)

    presentation = build_presentation(summary, trace)
    write_text(out_dir / REPORT_FILE, presentation)

    log_text = build_log(trace, out_dir, global_status)
    write_text(out_dir / CONTROL_FILE, log_text)

    print("=" * 72)
    print("RP9 RX8 GENEALOGICAL VALIDATOR")
    print("WHAT IS TESTED: Rx8 as a genealogical derivation from the first relation.")
    print("HOW IT IS TESTED: every later layer must be derived and may not claim origin status.")
    print("WHY IT IS TESTED: relation before projection must be locked operationally.")
    print("FINAL RESULT:", global_status)
    print("OUTPUT:", out_dir)

    for record in trace:
        print(record["step_id"] + " | " + record["status"] + " | " + record["title"] + " | " + record["final_result"])

    print("=" * 72)

    if not global_pass:
        return 1
    return 0

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-

# RP9_RX8_PROPORTION_STRUCTURE_VALIDATOR.py
# Version: 1.1.0
# Purpose:
# Independently validate the assigned Rx8 closure, structural, proportional,
# and residual controls defined inside this code.
#
# IMPORTANT BOUNDARY:
# 1/3 <-> 2/3 and 1/4 <-> 3/4 are tested as separate complementary closures.
# They are NOT treated as the same internal proportion.

# Proportion preservation is tested only where proportional identity is

# 3/4 <-> 1/4  ->  0.75 <-> 0.25.

# This code is self-contained. It does not require another RP9 code,
# validator, controller, output file, or execution phase.

import json
import math
import sys
from datetime import datetime
from fractions import Fraction
from pathlib import Path


PYTHON_CODE_ID = 'RX8. B'
FILE_NAME = 'RX8. B.py'
OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE = 'RX8. RP9 RX8 PROPORTION STRUCTURE VALIDATOR'
SCRIPT_VERSION = '1.1.0'

OUTPUT_DIR_NAME = '2. OUTPUT'
DATA_FILE = 'RX8.B_DATA.json'
TRACE_FILE = 'RX8.B_TRACE.json'
AUDIT_FILE = 'RX8.B_AUDIT.json'
VERIFY_FILE = 'RX8.B_VERIFY.json'
REPORT_FILE = 'RX8.B_REPORT.md'
CONTROL_FILE = 'RX8.B_CONTROL.txt'


def now_iso():
    return datetime.now().isoformat(timespec='seconds')


def make_output_dir():
    out_dir = Path.cwd() / OUTPUT_DIR_NAME
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return out_dir


def write_text(path, content):
    path.write_text(content, encoding='utf-8')


def write_json(path, data):
    path.write_text(
        json.dumps(data, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False),
        encoding='utf-8'
    )


def to_jsonable(value):
    if isinstance(value, Fraction):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, Path):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(k): to_jsonable(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [to_jsonable(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, tuple):
        return [to_jsonable(v) for v in value]
    return value


def status(pass_value):
    return 'PASS' if pass_value else 'FAIL'


def make_test_record(
    test_id,
    title,
    what_is_tested,
    how_it_is_tested,
    why_it_is_tested,
    expected_result,
    observed_result,
    passed,
    data
):
    return {
        'test_id': test_id,
        'title': title,
        'what_is_tested': what_is_tested,
        'how_it_is_tested': how_it_is_tested,
        'why_it_is_tested': why_it_is_tested,
        'expected_result': expected_result,
        'observed_result': observed_result,
        'final_result': status(passed),
        'data': to_jsonable(data)
    }


def test_1_relational_closure():
    left = Fraction(1, 3)
    right = Fraction(2, 3)
    total = left + right
    passed = total == Fraction(1, 1)

    return make_test_record(
        'TEST_1',
        'RELATIONAL_CLOSURE',
        'Complementary closure of the relation 1/3 <-> 2/3.',
        'Calculate 1/3 + 2/3 with exact rational arithmetic.',
        'To verify that this assigned relational pair closes exactly to one whole.',
        'The sum must be exactly 1.',
        'Observed exact sum: ' + str(total) + '.',
        passed,
        {
            'left': left,
            'right': right,
            'sum': total,
            'closure_target': Fraction(1, 1),
            'layer': 'RELATION',
            'test_function': 'COMPLEMENTARY_CLOSURE'
        }
    )


def test_2_representational_closure():
    reference = Fraction(1, 4)
    active = Fraction(3, 4)
    total = reference + active
    passed = total == Fraction(1, 1)

    return make_test_record(
        'TEST_2',
        'REPRESENTATIONAL_CLOSURE',
        'Complementary closure of the representation 1/4 <-> 3/4.',
        'Calculate 1/4 + 3/4 with exact rational arithmetic.',
        'To verify that this assigned representational pair closes exactly to one whole.',
        'The sum must be exactly 1.',
        'Observed exact sum: ' + str(total) + '.',
        passed,
        {
            'reference': reference,
            'active': active,
            'sum': total,
            'closure_target': Fraction(1, 1),
            'layer': 'REPRESENTATION',
            'test_function': 'COMPLEMENTARY_CLOSURE'
        }
    )


def test_3_rx8_capsulation():
    r_symbol = 'R'
    diameter_coefficient = Fraction(2, 1)
    square_sides = 4
    perimeter_coefficient = diameter_coefficient * square_sides
    expected = Fraction(8, 1)
    passed = perimeter_coefficient == expected

    return make_test_record(
        'TEST_3',
        'RX8_STRUCTURAL_CAPSULATION',
        'Rx8 structural capsulation: 2R x 4 = 8R.',
        'Multiply the symbolic diameter coefficient 2 by four square sides.',
        'To verify the assigned Rx8 structural coefficient without assigning a numerical magnitude to R.',
        'The perimeter coefficient must be exactly 8.',
        'Observed perimeter coefficient: ' + str(perimeter_coefficient) + ', representing 8R.',
        passed,
        {
            'R_status': 'SYMBOLIC_NOT_MEASURED',
            'R_symbol': r_symbol,
            'diameter': '2R',
            'square_sides': square_sides,
            'calculation': '2R * 4 = 8R',
            'perimeter_coefficient': perimeter_coefficient,
            'expected_coefficient': expected,
            'layer': 'STRUCTURE_RECONSTRUCTION'
        }
    )


def test_4_proportion_preservation():
    exact_active = Fraction(3, 4)
    exact_reference = Fraction(1, 4)
    decimal_active = 0.75
    decimal_reference = 0.25

    active_preserved = float(exact_active) == decimal_active
    reference_preserved = float(exact_reference) == decimal_reference
    exact_sum_preserved = exact_active + exact_reference == Fraction(1, 1)
    decimal_sum_preserved = decimal_active + decimal_reference == 1.0

    exact_ratio = exact_active / exact_reference
    decimal_ratio = decimal_active / decimal_reference
    ratio_preserved = decimal_ratio == float(exact_ratio)

    passed = (
        active_preserved
        and reference_preserved
        and exact_sum_preserved
        and decimal_sum_preserved
        and ratio_preserved
    )

    return make_test_record(
        'TEST_4',
        'PROPORTION_PRESERVATION',
        'Preservation of 3/4 <-> 1/4 as 0.75 <-> 0.25.',
        'Compare exact values, complementary closure, and the internal ratio before and after decimal representation.',
        'To verify actual proportional identity across this specific representational transformation.',
        '3/4 -> 0.75, 1/4 -> 0.25, both sums must equal 1, and both internal ratios must equal 3.',
        (
            'Observed exact ratio: '
            + str(exact_ratio)
            + '; decimal ratio: '
            + str(decimal_ratio)
            + '; decimal sum: '
            + str(decimal_active + decimal_reference)
            + '.'
        ),
        passed,
        {
            'exact_active': exact_active,
            'exact_reference': exact_reference,
            'decimal_active': decimal_active,
            'decimal_reference': decimal_reference,
            'exact_sum': exact_active + exact_reference,
            'decimal_sum': decimal_active + decimal_reference,
            'exact_ratio': exact_ratio,
            'decimal_ratio': decimal_ratio,
            'active_preserved': active_preserved,
            'reference_preserved': reference_preserved,
            'exact_sum_preserved': exact_sum_preserved,
            'decimal_sum_preserved': decimal_sum_preserved,
            'ratio_preserved': ratio_preserved,
            'test_function': 'PROPORTIONAL_IDENTITY'
        }
    )


def test_5_residual_position():
    exact_ratio = Fraction(3, 4)
    exact_lock = Fraction(1, 4)

    ri_float = math.sqrt(3.0) / 2.0
    observed_ratio = ri_float * ri_float
    observed_lock = 1.0 - observed_ratio

    expected_ratio = float(exact_ratio)
    expected_lock = float(exact_lock)

    ratio_residual = observed_ratio - expected_ratio
    lock_residual = observed_lock - expected_lock
    residual_sum = ratio_residual + lock_residual

    symmetric_residual = math.isclose(
        residual_sum,
        0.0,
        rel_tol=0.0,
        abs_tol=1e-30
    )
    exact_relation_intact = (
        exact_ratio + exact_lock == Fraction(1, 1)
    )

    passed = symmetric_residual and exact_relation_intact

    return make_test_record(
        'TEST_5',
        'RESIDUAL_POSITION',
        'Residual position between the exact 3/4 <-> 1/4 reference and its machine-computed geometric representation.',
        'Compute sqrt(3)/2 in binary floating point, square it, compare it with exact 3/4, and isolate the complementary residual pair.',
        'To verify that the machine-representation residual is symmetric while the exact complementary reference remains intact.',
        'The residual pair must sum to zero within the assigned tolerance, and the exact 3/4 + 1/4 relation must remain exactly 1.',
        (
            'Ratio residual: '
            + format(ratio_residual, '.20e')
            + '; lock residual: '
            + format(lock_residual, '.20e')
            + '; residual sum: '
            + format(residual_sum, '.20e')
            + '.'
        ),
        passed,
        {
            'exact_ratio': exact_ratio,
            'exact_lock': exact_lock,
            'exact_sum': exact_ratio + exact_lock,
            'ri_float': format(ri_float, '.20e'),
            'observed_ratio_float': format(observed_ratio, '.20e'),
            'observed_lock_float': format(observed_lock, '.20e'),
            'expected_ratio_float': format(expected_ratio, '.20e'),
            'expected_lock_float': format(expected_lock, '.20e'),
            'ratio_residual': format(ratio_residual, '.20e'),
            'lock_residual': format(lock_residual, '.20e'),
            'residual_sum': format(residual_sum, '.20e'),
            'symmetric_residual': symmetric_residual,
            'exact_relation_intact': exact_relation_intact,
            'layer': 'REPRESENTATION_TRACE'
        }
    )


def test_6_internal_validation(previous_tests):
    failed = [
        test
        for test in previous_tests
        if test['final_result'] != 'PASS'
    ]
    passed = len(failed) == 0

    controls = [
        'RELATIONAL CLOSURE: 1/3 + 2/3 = 1',
        'REPRESENTATIONAL CLOSURE: 1/4 + 3/4 = 1',
        'RX8 STRUCTURE: 2R x 4 = 8R',
        'PROPORTION PRESERVATION: 3/4 <-> 1/4 = 0.75 <-> 0.25 with ratio 3:1 preserved',
        'RESIDUAL POSITION: symmetric machine-representation trace'
    ]

    return make_test_record(
        'TEST_6',
        'INTERNAL_VALIDATION_LOCK',
        'Combined status of the five independent internal controls executed by this code.',
        'Collect TEST_1 through TEST_5 and require every assigned control to return PASS.',
        'To provide one final status for this self-contained code without claiming that different mathematical relations share one invariant proportion.',
        'All five preceding internal controls must return PASS.',
        'Number of failed preceding controls: ' + str(len(failed)) + '.',
        passed,
        {
            'controls': controls,
            'failed_tests': [test['test_id'] for test in failed],
            'all_previous_tests_passed': passed,
            'scope': 'INTERNAL_TO_THIS_CODE_ONLY'
        }
    )

def build_control_log(summary, tests, out_dir):
    lines = []
    lines.append('RP9 RX8 PROPORTION STRUCTURE VALIDATOR CONTROL LOG')
    lines.append('Generated: ' + summary['generated_at'])
    lines.append('Python Code ID: ' + PYTHON_CODE_ID)
    lines.append('Official Code Title: ' + OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE)
    lines.append('File: ' + FILE_NAME)
    lines.append('Version: ' + summary['version'])
    lines.append('Output directory: ' + str(out_dir))
    lines.append('Global status: ' + summary['global_status'])
    lines.append('')

    for test in tests:
        lines.append(
            test['test_id']
            + ' | '
            + test['final_result']
            + ' | '
            + test['title']
        )
        lines.append('WHAT: ' + test['what_is_tested'])
        lines.append('HOW: ' + test['how_it_is_tested'])
        lines.append('WHY: ' + test['why_it_is_tested'])
        lines.append('RESULT: ' + test['observed_result'])
        lines.append('')

    return '\n'.join(lines)


def run_validator():
    out_dir = make_output_dir()

    tests = [
        test_1_relational_closure(),
        test_2_representational_closure(),
        test_3_rx8_capsulation(),
        test_4_proportion_preservation(),
        test_5_residual_position()
    ]
    tests.append(test_6_internal_validation(tests))

    global_pass = all(
        test['final_result'] == 'PASS'
        for test in tests
    )
    global_status = status(global_pass)

    summary = {
        'system': 'RP9_RX8',
        'validation': 'SELF_CONTAINED_PROPORTION_STRUCTURE_VALIDATION',
        'repository': 'RP9. RH. Z0',
        'repository_branch': '2. RP9. EXPANSION',
        'python_code_id': PYTHON_CODE_ID,
        'filesystem_name': FILE_NAME,
        'official_code_title': OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE,
        'version': SCRIPT_VERSION,
        'generated_at': now_iso(),
        'global_status': global_status,
        'code_independence': True,
        'external_rp9_code_dependency': False,
        'principle': (
            'Complementary closure and proportional identity are distinct '
            'validation functions.'
        ),
        'validation_boundary': (
            'This code validates only its internally assigned closure, '
            'Rx8 structural, proportional-preservation, and residual controls.'
        )
    }

    payload = {
        'SUMMARY': summary,
        'TESTS': tests
    }

    trace_payload = {
        'TRACE': tests
    }

    audit_payload = {
        'AUDIT': {
            'all_tests_include_what_how_why_result': all(
                all(
                    key in test
                    for key in [
                        'what_is_tested',
                        'how_it_is_tested',
                        'why_it_is_tested',
                        'final_result'
                    ]
                )
                for test in tests
            ),
            'self_contained_execution': True,
            'external_rp9_code_dependency': False,
            'relational_closure_separated_from_proportional_identity': True,
            'cross_relation_proportional_invariance_claimed': False,
            'global_status': global_status
        }
    }

    verify_payload = {
        'VERIFY': {
            'test_1_relational_closure':
                tests[0]['final_result'] == 'PASS',
            'test_2_representational_closure':
                tests[1]['final_result'] == 'PASS',
            'test_3_rx8_capsulation':
                tests[2]['final_result'] == 'PASS',
            'test_4_proportion_preservation':
                tests[3]['final_result'] == 'PASS',
            'test_5_residual_position':
                tests[4]['final_result'] == 'PASS',
            'test_6_internal_validation':
                tests[5]['final_result'] == 'PASS',
            'global_status': global_status
        }
    }

    write_json(
        out_dir / DATA_FILE,
        payload
    )
    write_json(
        out_dir / TRACE_FILE,
        trace_payload
    )
    write_json(
        out_dir / AUDIT_FILE,
        audit_payload
    )
    write_json(
        out_dir / VERIFY_FILE,
        verify_payload
    )

    markdown = build_markdown(summary, tests)
    write_text(
        out_dir / REPORT_FILE,
        markdown
    )

    control_log = build_control_log(summary, tests, out_dir)
    write_text(
        out_dir / CONTROL_FILE,
        control_log
    )

    print('=' * 72)
    print('RP9 RX8 PROPORTION STRUCTURE VALIDATOR')
    print('STATUS:', global_status)
    print('OUTPUT:', out_dir)
    print('=' * 72)

    for test in tests:
        print(
            test['test_id']
            + ' | '
            + test['final_result']
            + ' | '
            + test['title']
        )

    print('=' * 72)

    return 0 if global_pass else 1


if __name__ == '__main__':
    exit_code = run_validator()
    sys.exit(exit_code)

META-ABSTRACT

META-ABSTRACT

This package provides a self-contained executable validator for selected complementary, binary-scale and positional value relations within RP9.

It checks exact rational identities, projects selected rational values into machine representation and records the status of its internal controls.

Its assigned operation is:

SELECTED VALUE RELATION⟶EXECUTABLE CONTROL⟶RECORDED RESULT

The selected rational positions are defined within the script. The calculations test the identities and transformations implemented for those positions.

Go to: ⟶ NAVIGATION & LINKS

RP9 🜁 — NAVIGATION & LINKS 🔗

📂 — 2. RP9. EXPANSION

🜁 — Links 🔗

📂 000. A.P.X. 2

  • 🔗NAVIGATION & LINKS

PURPOSE AND EXECUTION MODEL

The validator performs six internal controls:

Control Function
TEST_1 — COMPLEMENTARY_VALUE_RELATION Checks closure and complement for 14 and 34.
TEST_2 — BINARY_SCALE_EXTENSION Generates and checks the positions 1,12,14,18 through the binary scale rule.
TEST_3 — SCALE_INVARIANT_COMPLEMENT Checks complementary closure and the ratio 3 :1 at four selected scales.
TEST_4 — SEVEN_PLUS_ONE_POSITION_RELATION Calculates the total 7 +1 =8 and its normalized complementary positions.
TEST_5 — REPRESENTATIONAL_PROJECTION Converts five exact rational positions to float and records recovered values and residuals.
TEST_6 — INTERNAL_VALIDATION_LOCK Requires all five preceding internal controls to report PASS.

Each test record includes what is tested, how it is tested, why it is tested, its expected result, its observed result and its status.

The script uses Python's standard library. Its controls execute without another RP9 validator, external data files or a geometric construction.

EXACT RELATIONS

Exact calculations use fractions.Fraction.

The complementary control checks:

14+34=1,1−14=34.

The binary scale positions are:

1,12,14,18.

For each selected nonzero scale 𝑆, the scale control checks:

𝑆4+3𝑆4=𝑆,3𝑆/4𝑆/4=3.

The tested scales are:

𝑆∈{1,2,8,18}.

The positional control uses the assigned values 7 and 1, calculates their total and checks:

7+1=8,78+18=1.

MACHINE REPRESENTATION AND RESIDUAL RECORDS

TEST_5 preserves each exact rational source value and separately records its float representation.

The machine value is recovered as an exact fraction using Fraction.from_float. The recorded residual is:

𝛿repr=recovered machine value−exact source value.

The supplied execution records contain:

Exact source Float value Recovered fraction Recorded residual
12 0.5 1/2 0
14 0.25 1/4 0
34 0.75 3/4 0
18 0.125 1/8 0
78 0.875 7/8 0

These selected fractions have exact finite binary representations. Their direct conversions therefore preserve the source values in the supplied records.

The PASS condition for this control checks that all five projections have been recorded and contain float values. The residual values remain explicit data; zero residual is not a separate enforced PASS condition.

Location Content and function

2. OUTPUT/RX8.C_AUDIT.json Execution metadata and internal audit fields.
2. OUTPUT/RX8.C_CONTROL.txt Readable control log with test descriptions and statuses.

2. OUTPUT/RX8.C_REPORT.md Readable execution report.

2. OUTPUT/RX8.C_VERIFY.json Boolean control statuses and global status.
3. FINAL REPORTS/RX8.C_REPORT.md Retained copy of the supplied execution report.

The machine-readable merged file brings the README, Python source and supplied output documents together for inspection.

VERIFY summarizes the script's internal test statuses. TRACE contains structured test records. These files document the same execution.

HOW TO RUN

Use Python 3 and run the following command from the root of 3. RP9. RX8:

python "1. Python/RX8. C.py"

The output directory is resolved relative to the current working directory:

Path.cwd() / "2. OUTPUT"

Running from the package root places the six generated output files in the package's 2. OUTPUT directory. Subsequent runs overwrite the matching output filenames.

The script returns exit code 0 when the global status is PASS and 1 when it is FAIL.

The report in 3. FINAL REPORTS is a retained copy. The script writes its report to 2. OUTPUT; updating the retained copy is a separate file operation.

SUPPLIED EXECUTION RESULT

RELATION TO THE RP9 ARCHITECTURE

Within C. CODE ARCHITECTURE, this package supplies executable controls for its selected exact complementary relations, binary scale positions, scale transformations and machine projections.

Its result applies to the six controls implemented in RX8. C.py. The code establishes their execution status independently of the execution status of other RP9 packages.

The package preserves the distinction between the exact source relation, its machine representation and the residual recorded for that representation.

CONTROL_FILE = "RX8.C_CONTROL.txt"


def now_iso():
    return datetime.now().isoformat(timespec="seconds")


def make_output_dir():
    out_dir = Path.cwd() / OUTPUT_DIR_NAME
    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    return out_dir


def write_text(path, content):
    path.write_text(content, encoding="utf-8")


def write_json(path, data):
    path.write_text(
        json.dumps(data, indent=4, ensure_ascii=False),
        encoding="utf-8"
    )


def to_jsonable(value):
    if isinstance(value, Fraction):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, Path):
        return str(value)
    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {str(k): to_jsonable(v) for k, v in value.items()}
    if isinstance(value, list):
        return [to_jsonable(v) for v in value]
    if isinstance(value, tuple):
        return [to_jsonable(v) for v in value]
    return value


def status(pass_value):
    return "PASS" if pass_value else "FAIL"


def make_test_record(
    test_id,
    title,
    what_is_tested,
    how_it_is_tested,
    why_it_is_tested,
    expected_result,
    observed_result,
    passed,
    data,
):
    return {
        "test_id": test_id,
        "title": title,
        "what_is_tested": what_is_tested,
        "how_it_is_tested": how_it_is_tested,
        "why_it_is_tested": why_it_is_tested,
        "expected_result": expected_result,
        "observed_result": observed_result,
        "result": status(passed),
        "data": to_jsonable(data),
    }


def test_1_complementary_value_relation():
    left = Fraction(1, 4)
    right = Fraction(3, 4)
    whole = left + right

    passed = whole == 1 and right == 1 - left

    return make_test_record(
        "TEST_1",
        "COMPLEMENTARY_VALUE_RELATION",
        "The complementary value relation 1/4 and 3/4 within one preserved whole.",
        "Uses exact rational arithmetic and checks both closure and complement.",
        "To verify the relation as a value identity without assigning it to a geometric form.",
        "1/4 + 3/4 = 1 and 3/4 = 1 - 1/4.",
        f"Whole = {whole}; complement of 1/4 = {1-left}.",
        passed,
        {
            "left_position": left,
            "right_position": right,
            "whole": whole,
            "closure": left + right,
            "complement_of_left": 1 - left,
        },
    )


def test_2_binary_scale_extension():
    start = Fraction(1, 1)
    positions = [start / (2 ** n) for n in range(4)]
    expected = [
        Fraction(1, 1),
        Fraction(1, 2),
        Fraction(1, 4),
        Fraction(1, 8),
    ]

    passed = positions == expected

    return make_test_record(
        "TEST_2",
        "BINARY_SCALE_EXTENSION",
        "Repeated binary scaling of one established value.",
        "Applies the same division-by-two operation recursively with exact rational arithmetic.",
        "To verify that later scale positions are generated by the same operation rather than by a new rule.",
        "1 -> 1/2 -> 1/4 -> 1/8.",
        "Generated positions: " + " -> ".join(str(v) for v in positions) + ".",
        passed,
        {
            "operation": "x 1/2",
            "positions": positions,
            "expected_positions": expected,
        },
    )


def test_3_scale_invariant_complement():
    scales = [Fraction(1, 1), Fraction(2, 1), Fraction(8, 1), Fraction(1, 8)]
    records = []
    passed = True

    for scale in scales:
        left = scale * Fraction(1, 4)
        right = scale * Fraction(3, 4)
        total = left + right
        ratio = right / left

        local_pass = total == scale and ratio == 3
        passed = passed and local_pass

        records.append({
            "scale": scale,
            "left": left,
            "right": right,
            "total": total,
            "right_to_left_ratio": ratio,
            "pass": local_pass,
        })

    return make_test_record(
        "TEST_3",
        "SCALE_INVARIANT_COMPLEMENT",
        "The 1/4 and 3/4 complementary relation under multiple exact scales.",
        "Scales both positions by the same factor and checks closure and the 3:1 ratio.",
        "To verify that scale changes the magnitude of the positions without changing their internal relation.",
        "For every tested scale S: S/4 + 3S/4 = S and (3S/4)/(S/4) = 3.",
        f"Checked {len(records)} exact scales; all preserved closure and ratio.",
        passed,
        {
            "tested_scales": records,
            "invariant_ratio": Fraction(3, 1),
        },
    )


def test_4_seven_plus_one_position_relation():
    active = 7
    reference = 1
    total = active + reference
    active_ratio = Fraction(active, total)
    reference_ratio = Fraction(reference, total)

    passed = (
        total == 8
        and active_ratio == Fraction(7, 8)
        and reference_ratio == Fraction(1, 8)
        and active_ratio + reference_ratio == 1
    )

    return make_test_record(
        "TEST_4",
        "SEVEN_PLUS_ONE_POSITION_RELATION",
        "The positional value relation 7 + 1 within a total of 8.",
        "Computes the total and the exact relative positions 7/8 and 1/8.",
        "To verify the value relation independently of any geometric interpretation.",
        "7 + 1 = 8; 7/8 + 1/8 = 1.",
        f"Total = {total}; active = {active_ratio}; reference = {reference_ratio}.",
        passed,
        {
            "active_value": active,
            "reference_value": reference,
            "total": total,
            "active_ratio": active_ratio,
            "reference_ratio": reference_ratio,
            "closure": active_ratio + reference_ratio,
        },
    )


def test_5_representational_projection():
    exact_positions = [
        Fraction(1, 2),
        Fraction(1, 4),
        Fraction(3, 4),
        Fraction(1, 8),
        Fraction(7, 8),
    ]

    records = []
    passed = True

    for value in exact_positions:
        decimal_value = float(value)
        recovered = Fraction.from_float(decimal_value)
        residual = recovered - value

        records.append({
            "exact_value": value,
            "decimal_value": decimal_value,
            "recovered_fraction": recovered,
            "residual": residual,
        })

        if not isinstance(decimal_value, float):
            passed = False

    return make_test_record(
        "TEST_5",
        "REPRESENTATIONAL_PROJECTION",
        "Projection of selected exact rational positions into machine decimal representation.",
        "Converts exact rational values to float and records the exact recovered machine value and residual.",
        "To keep exact functional values separate from their machine representation.",
        "Every selected exact position is projected and its representation residual is explicitly recorded.",
        f"Projected {len(records)} exact positions and recorded all residuals.",
        passed and len(records) == len(exact_positions),
        {
            "projection_records": records,
            "exact_values_remain_source_values": True,
        },
    )


def test_6_internal_validation_lock(previous_tests):
    failed = [test["test_id"] for test in previous_tests if test["result"] != "PASS"]
    passed = len(failed) == 0

    return make_test_record(
        "TEST_6",
        "INTERNAL_VALIDATION_LOCK",
        "The combined status of TEST_1 through TEST_5 inside this validator.",
        "Collects the five independent internal test results and requires all of them to PASS.",
        "To provide one final status for this self-contained code without depending on another RP9 validator.",
        "TEST_1 through TEST_5 must all be PASS.",
        f"Failed internal tests: {failed}.",
        passed,
        {
            "failed_tests": failed,
            "all_previous_tests_passed": passed,
            "external_rp9_code_dependency": False,
        },
    )


def build_markdown(summary, tests):
    lines = [
        "> [!info] **RP9. CODE IDENTITY**",
        "> ",
        "> - ### REPOSITORY: _**RP9. RH. Z0**_",
        ">     ",
        ">     - #### **2. RP9. EXPANSION**",
        ">",
        ">---",
        f"> - PYTHON CODE 🆔: **{PYTHON_CODE_ID}**",
        "> ",
        f"> - OFFICIAL CODE TITEL: **{OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE}**",
        "> ",
        ">---",
        "",
        "# RP9 RX8 FUNCTIONAL RELATION VALIDATOR",
        "",
        "## GLOBAL RESULT",
        "",
        "```text",
        "STATUS: " + summary["global_status"],
        "PYTHON CODE ID: " + PYTHON_CODE_ID,
        "OFFICIAL CODE TITLE: " + OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE,
        "VERSION: " + summary["version"],
        "GENERATED: " + summary["generated_at"],
        "```",
        "",
        "---",
        "",
        "## PURPOSE",
        "",
        "This validator is self-contained.",
        "",
        "It validates selected functional, relational, positional and value identities",
        "without requiring geometric structures or another RP9 validator.",
        "",
        "---",
        "",
        "## VALIDATION MODEL",
        "",
        "```text",
        "EXACT VALUE RELATION",
        "        |",
        "        v",
        "BINARY SCALE EXTENSION",
        "        |",
        "        v",
        "SCALE-INVARIANT COMPLEMENT",
        "        |",
        "        v",
        "POSITIONAL VALUE RELATION",
        "        |",
        "        v",
        "REPRESENTATIONAL PROJECTION",
        "        |",
        "        v",
        "INTERNAL VALIDATION LOCK",
        "```",
        "",
        "---",
        "",
    ]

    for test in tests:
        lines.extend([
            "## " + test["test_id"] + " — " + test["title"],
            "",
            "### What is tested",
            "",
            test["what_is_tested"],
            "",
            "### How it is tested",
            "",
            test["how_it_is_tested"],
            "",
            "### Why it is tested",
            "",
            test["why_it_is_tested"],
            "",
            "### Expected result",
            "",
            test["expected_result"],
            "",
            "### Observed result",
            "",
            test["observed_result"],
            "",
            "### Result",
            "",
            "```text",
            test["result"],
            "```",
            "",
            "---",
            "",
        ])

    lines.extend([
        "## CONCLUSION",
        "",
        "All assigned internal controls passed."
        if summary["global_status"] == "PASS"
        else "At least one assigned internal control failed.",
        "",
        "The result belongs to this validator only and does not require",
        "a preceding or subsequent RP9 code to establish its execution status.",
        "",
    ])

    return "\n".join(lines)


def build_control_log(summary, tests, out_dir):
    lines = [
        "RP9 RX8 FUNCTIONAL RELATION VALIDATOR CONTROL LOG",
        "Generated: " + summary["generated_at"],
        "Python Code ID: " + PYTHON_CODE_ID,
        "Official Code Title: " + OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE,
        "File: " + FILE_NAME,
        "Version: " + summary["version"],
        "Output directory: " + str(out_dir),
        "Global status: " + summary["global_status"],
        "",
    ]

    for test in tests:
        lines.extend([
            test["test_id"] + " | " + test["result"] + " | " + test["title"],
            "WHAT: " + test["what_is_tested"],
            "HOW: " + test["how_it_is_tested"],
            "WHY: " + test["why_it_is_tested"],
            "RESULT: " + test["observed_result"],
            "",
        ])

    return "\n".join(lines)


def run_validator():
    out_dir = make_output_dir()

    tests = [
        test_1_complementary_value_relation(),
        test_2_binary_scale_extension(),
        test_3_scale_invariant_complement(),
        test_4_seven_plus_one_position_relation(),
        test_5_representational_projection(),
    ]
    tests.append(test_6_internal_validation_lock(tests))

    global_pass = all(test["result"] == "PASS" for test in tests)
    global_status = status(global_pass)

    summary = {
        "system": "RP9_RX8",
        "validation": "FUNCTIONAL_RELATION_VALIDATION",
        "repository": "RP9. RH. Z0",
        "repository_branch": "2. RP9. EXPANSION",
        "python_code_id": PYTHON_CODE_ID,
        "filesystem_name": FILE_NAME,
        "official_code_title": OFFICIAL_CODE_TITLE,
        "version": SCRIPT_VERSION,
        "generated_at": now_iso(),
        "global_status": global_status,
        "self_contained_execution": True,
        "external_rp9_code_dependency": False,
        "principle": "Function, relation, position and value are validated without geometric structure requirements.",
        "validation_boundary": "Only the identities explicitly calculated by this code are claimed as validated.",
    }

    payload = {
        "SUMMARY": summary,
        "TESTS": tests,
    }

    trace_payload = {
        "TRACE": tests,
    }

    audit_payload = {
        "AUDIT": {
            "all_tests_include_what_how_why_result": all(
                all(
                    key in test
                    for key in [
                        "what_is_tested",
                        "how_it_is_tested",
                        "why_it_is_tested",
                        "result",
                    ]
                )
                for test in tests
            ),
            "self_contained_execution": True,
            "external_rp9_code_dependency": False,
            "geometric_structure_required": False,
            "phase_dependency_required": False,
            "only_explicitly_calculated_identities_claimed": True,
            "global_status": global_status,
        }
    }

    verify_payload = {
        "VERIFY": {
            "test_1_complementary_value_relation": tests[0]["result"] == "PASS",
            "test_2_binary_scale_extension": tests[1]["result"] == "PASS",
            "test_3_scale_invariant_complement": tests[2]["result"] == "PASS",
            "test_4_seven_plus_one_position_relation": tests[3]["result"] == "PASS",
            "test_5_representational_projection": tests[4]["result"] == "PASS",
            "test_6_internal_validation_lock": tests[5]["result"] == "PASS",
            "global_status": global_status,
        }
    }

    write_json(out_dir / DATA_FILE, payload)
    write_json(out_dir / TRACE_FILE, trace_payload)
    write_json(out_dir / AUDIT_FILE, audit_payload)
    write_json(out_dir / VERIFY_FILE, verify_payload)

    markdown = build_markdown(summary, tests)
    write_text(out_dir / REPORT_FILE, markdown)

    control_log = build_control_log(summary, tests, out_dir)
    write_text(out_dir / CONTROL_FILE, control_log)

    print("=" * 72)
    print("RP9 RX8 FUNCTIONAL RELATION VALIDATOR")
    print("STATUS:", global_status)
    print("OUTPUT:", out_dir)
    print("=" * 72)
    for test in tests:
        print(test["test_id"] + " | " + test["result"] + " | " + test["title"])
    print("=" * 72)

    return 0 if global_pass else 1


if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(run_validator())

This folder contains the executable and generated output for the self-contained:

PYTHON CODE ID: RX8. D

OFFICIAL CODE TITLE: RX8. RP9 RX8 RESIDUAL VALIDATOR

Its assigned function is to independently compare:

and

EXECUTED NUMERICAL REPRESENTATIONS

and measure any residual difference produced by the representation.

The validator therefore operates on:

+

It does not require another RP9 code, validator, controller, output file, or execution phase in order to perform its assigned controls.

2. Validation boundary

The validator tests only the residual and representation properties that it calculates directly.

=
MEASURED NUMERICAL DIFFERENCE

AND AN EXECUTED REPRESENTATION

The code does not require:

GENEALOGY VALIDATION

STRUCTURE VALIDATION

A CROSS-CODE CONTROLLER

# -*- coding: utf-8 -*-
# RP9_CODE_ID: C.0073
# =============================================================================
